interpretation: It is impossible that the mover which is itself moved by another should go on to infinity, since among infinitely many there is no first (ἀδύνατον γὰρ εἰς ἄπειρον ἰέναι τὸ κινοῦν καὶ κινούμενον ὑπʼ ἄλλου αὐτό· τῶν γὰρ ἀπείρων οὐκ ἔστιν οὐδὲν πρῶτον). Formalized as well-foundedness of the link 'moves this thing, is another than it, and is itself moved by another'. Unlike the prima via's regress premise it is not restricted to per se links; the chapter's stick-hand-man example (256a6-13) illustrates it, and the per accidens case is taken up only from 256b3. Scope: Aristotle's physical motion; the Lean has no guard, so the reading is accepted only under a physical instantiation of `MovedIn`/`MovesIn` (DISAMB-MOTION). `Acc` also excludes finite cycles of movers and is stronger than denying an infinite descending chain; the sentence speaks only of going to infinity. The corpus uses the same well-foundedness form for the prima via's 'non est procedere in infinitum' (STMT-NO-INFINITE-PER-SE-MOVER-SERIES); the extra strength is a property of that formalization convention, not something Aristotle says. A narrower sibling reading restricted to the instrumental series of 256a4-13 (movers that move because they are moved) is defensible and not formalized; it would weaken the premise and leave ARIST-PHYS-VIII-5-FIRST-MOVER-NOT-MOVED-BY-ANOTHER without its induction step for other movers moved by another.
